checks: every kept row identical (d1, d2, h) in the three independent sources (fasteners.eu, globalfastener, schrauben-lexikon)
d1 > thread diameter in every row (d1 - d from 0.1 mm at M1.6 to 1.0 mm at M30; 1.0 mm for M12 and up)
d1 and d2 strictly increase with size; h never decreases (0.3, 0.5, 1, 1.6, 2, 2.5, 3, 4 mm steps)
d2 > d1 everywhere; d2/d1 between 1.54 and 2.06 (small series: OD about 1.5-2.1 x hole)
no row where ISO 7092 and DIN 433 differ is published (M18 h: ISO 3 vs DIN 2.5; M36 d2: ISO 60 vs DIN 58)
shape_hint: A thin flat round washer: disc with a concentric through-hole, flat on both faces, product grade A (hole slightly larger than the screw thread); small outside diameter (about 1.5-2.1 times the hole), intended for cheese-head screws.

role_map.d_nom_note: thread size M that the washer fits (ISO 7092 names the washer by thread size; DIN 433 named it by hole size)

notes: Rows are the intersection of three independent public tables; limit (max/min) columns omitted. M3.5 and M14 are bracketed (non-preferred) sizes of the standard but are listed identically in all sources. Dropped on purpose: M18 (h) and M36 (d2), where ISO 7092 (3 / 60 per globalfastener + schrauben-lexikon + boltport) and DIN 433 (2.5 / 58 per fasteners.eu, globalfastener DIN 433-1) differ - one more independent ISO 7092 source would make them publishable; and M22, M27, M33 (not on fasteners.eu). boltport.com pages mirror schrauben-lexikon and fasteners.eu data and were not counted as sources.

verification.checks_done: Live re-fetch + python parse of fasteners.eu ISO 7092 and DIN 433, torqbolt DIN 433, globalfastener detail_230 (ISO) and detail_623 (DIN), schrauben-lexikon ISO_7092, boltport iso-7092 and din-433. Matrix 27 thread sizes x (d1,d2,h) x 8 pages. All 16 kept rows (M1.6,M2,M2.5,M3,M3.5,M4,M5,M6,M8,M10,M12,M14,M16,M20,M24,M30) x 3 cols are identical in fe, gf_iso and sl_iso (48/48 cells, 3 clusters each), and equal in fe_din/gf_din/tq_din. Verified the ISO vs DIN differences are exactly M18 h (ISO 3 / DIN 2.5) and M36 d2 (ISO 60 / DIN 58): fasteners.eu ISO page = DIN 433 table (fe_iso == fe_din on all 22 rows incl. 2.5 and 58), gf_iso/sl_iso/boltport_iso give 3 and 60. No other ISO != DIN difference exists in any kept row. Headers read from the pages: 'd min = nominal size', 'dc max = nominal size', 'h Nominal size' (gf), 'd1 min / d2 max / h Nominal size' (fe). Physical sanity: d1 and d2 strictly increase, h non-decreasing, d2 > d1, d1 > thread dia.
problems: STRICT reading: every kept cell has EXACTLY 3 clusters (fe-cluster, gf, sl); no margin. If boltport were the 3rd instead of fasteners.eu it would not help (boltport = fe cluster per lead; also copies sl).

ISO-proper support is only gf_iso + sl_iso (+boltport ISO page, same cluster as fe) : the fasteners.eu 'ISO 7092' page is literally the DIN 433 table (identical to /DIN/433/ in all 22 rows, so it prints DIN numbers). It is accepted only because for the 16 kept rows DIN 433 == ISO 7092 numerically. If the lead wants 3 clusters carrying genuine ISO-labelled numbers independent of the DIN table, pws has 2 (gf, sl) and would fail.

M18 (h) and M36 (d2) correctly dropped: the fe cluster is internally inconsistent there (fasteners.eu 2.5/58 vs boltport 3/60), ISO values 3/60 have only gf + sl = 2 clusters. M22, M27, M33 correctly dropped (not on fasteners.eu: gf + sl only). M1, M1.2, M1.4, M1.8 (not in gf), M2.2, M7 (sl only) correctly dropped.

globalfastener tables carry no thread label (only d, dc, h); the M label of each gf column is matched through the hole diameter d1 (unique per row), not read from a header. Verified unique for all 16 rows.
boltport DIN 433 page has a typo M1.2 d1 = 1.5 (irrelevant: row dropped, boltport not counted).
M3.5 and M14 are bracketed non-preferred sizes in ISO 7092 but listed identically in all three clusters.

standard_full: ISO 7092:2000 (plain washers, small series, product grade A; = DIN EN ISO 7092 = DIN 433 for the rows kept)
